usdRate.sourceName: European Central Bank euro reference rate (USD)
usdRate.note: EUR 1 = USD 1.1172 on 30 October 2026 (ECB EXR dataset), so about EUR 0.895 per US dollar; World Bank 2025 average 0.885.

inflation_cpi.sourceName: LRT, reporting the State Data Agency (Valstybės duomenų agentūra) September 2026 CPI release
inflation_cpi.note: National CPI up 6.7% year on year in September 2026 (HICP 6.1%; 12-month average CPI 4.9%). Secondary source: the official statistics portal could not be read; Trading Economics reports the same 6.7%. World Bank 2025 average 3.8%.

inflation_projection.sourceName: ECB 2% medium-term target; Lithuanian CPI averaged about 7% a year in 2021-2025 (18.9% in 2022) and 6.7% in Sep 2026
inflation_projection.note: Lithuania shares the ECB 2% target but its prices and wages keep converging towards richer euro members and inflation is running well above target in 2026, so 3% is used for long-run planning.

policy_rate.sourceName: European Central Bank, key ECB interest rates (deposit facility)
policy_rate.note: Lithuania uses the euro; ECB deposit facility rate 2.50% since 16 September 2026 (2.25% from June 2026), confirmed in the ECB FM dataset on 31 October 2026.

savings_account_rate.sourceName: ECB MFI interest rate statistics: Lithuanian banks, overnight deposits from households (new business)
savings_account_rate.note: Average rate on household overnight deposits in Lithuania, September 2026 (0.25% in August and July).

fdr_3m_rate.note: ECB/Bank of Lithuania MFI statistics publish household deposits with agreed maturity up to 1 year as one bucket (2.34% in September 2026); no separate 3-month term deposit rate was found.

fdr_1y_rate.sourceName: ECB MFI interest rate statistics: Lithuanian banks, household deposits with agreed maturity up to 1 year (new business)
fdr_1y_rate.note: Bucket covers all fixed terms up to one year (2.43% in August, 2.07% in July); deposits of over 1 and up to 2 years paid 3.60% in September 2026 (ECB MIR M.LT.B.L22.G).

dps_rate.note: Lithuanian banks offer regular savings deposits (kaupiamasis indėlis), but no average or official rate for them was found in Bank of Lithuania or ECB statistics.

bank_deposit_avg_rate.sourceName: ECB MFI interest rate statistics: Lithuanian banks, household deposits with agreed maturity (outstanding amounts)
bank_deposit_avg_rate.note: Average rate on all outstanding household term deposits, September 2026 (2.12% in August); household overnight deposits paid 0.26%. World Bank FR.INR.DPST has no Lithuania figure.

sanchayapatra_5y_rate.note: Lithuania sells Government savings notes / defence bonds to individuals (terms up to 3 years, no 5-year note), but the current rate could not be confirmed: the Ministry of Finance pages return 403 to automated reading and the researcher's 3.4% (3-year, 27 Oct-9 Nov 2026 issue) came only from a search-result snippet.

tbill_91d_rate.note: No 3-month Lithuanian treasury bill yield was found; the Ministry of Finance's securities pages could not be read and the ECB publishes no Lithuanian money-market yield.

tbond_5y_rate.note: No current 5-year government bond yield from an official or allowed secondary source was found; a 5-year Eurobond tranche was issued in January 2026 but the Ministry of Finance release with its yield could not be read.

tbond_10y_rate.sourceName: Trading Economics, Lithuania 10-year government bond yield
tbond_10y_rate.note: Secondary source. The ECB long-term convergence rate for Lithuania shows 2.88% for July-September 2026 but has been flat for months, so the market yield is used.

tax_bank_interest.sourceName: PwC Worldwide Tax Summaries, Lithuania significant developments and taxes on personal income
tax_bank_interest.note: From 1 January 2026 almost all individual income is taxed at progressive 20%/25%/32% rates; the reduced 15% list (dividends, some pension and share income) does not include interest, so the 20% first band is used. The first EUR 500 of interest a year on deposits and securities is exempt (PwC income determination page). Some secondary sources still quote 15% for interest, so check before relying on it.

tax_sanchayapatra_profit.note: No readable official source on how interest on Government savings notes (defence bonds) is taxed was found; it is believed to follow the general interest rules (EUR 500 annual exemption), but the State Tax Inspectorate pages could not be read.

deposit_insurance_limit.sourceName: Indėlių ir investicijų draudimas (Deposit and Investment Insurance), deposit insurance
deposit_insurance_limit.note: EUR 100,000 per depositor per credit institution, all eligible deposits at one bank added together.

credit_card_rate_cap.sourceName: ECB MFI interest rate statistics: Lithuanian banks, revolving loans, overdrafts and credit card credit to households
credit_card_rate_cap.note: Typical rate, not a cap: average rate on household revolving loans, overdrafts and credit card credit, September 2026 (9.91% in August).

equity_return_low.sourceName: OMX Vilnius gross index 1,490 on 30 Oct 2026 (base 100 at end-1999), up 18.6% in a year
equity_return_low.note: Low case: the small, concentrated Vilnius market returns only a little more than safe savings over a long period.

equity_return_base.sourceName: OMX Vilnius (Trading Economics); 1-year deposit 2.34% less 20% tax = 1.87% (ECB MFI, Sep 2026)
equity_return_base.note: OMX Vilnius has compounded about 10% a year since 2000, but the market is small and illiquid, so the base uses a diversified euro equity fund and is held at the after-tax 1-year deposit rate plus about 4 points.

equity_return_high.sourceName: OMX Vilnius long-run record; long-run global equity returns
equity_return_high.note: High case: a diversified euro equity fund matching long-run global equity returns of about 8% in euros.

gold_return_low.note: Low case: gold barely keeps up after the 2025-26 spike, with no help from the euro.

gold_return_base.sourceName: Gold price history (Trading Economics); ECB 2% inflation target
gold_return_base.note: Base case: dollar gold rises roughly with world inflation plus a little, and the euro is assumed stable against the dollar over the long run.

gold_return_high.note: High case: a repeat of gold's strong 2005-2025 trend in euro terms.

fixed_income_return_low.sourceName: Household deposits up to 1 year 2.34% (ECB MFI statistics, Sep 2026), assuming rates fall, less 20% tax
fixed_income_return_low.note: Low case: term deposit and savings-note rates drift down towards 1.6% before the 20% tax.

fixed_income_return_base.sourceName: 1-year deposit 2.34% and 1-2 year deposit 3.60% less 20% tax = 1.9-2.9% (ECB MFI, Sep 2026)
fixed_income_return_base.note: Base case: a mix of term deposits up to 2 years after the 20% tax (the EUR 500 interest exemption makes small balances effectively tax-free).

fixed_income_return_high.sourceName: Household deposits over 1 and up to 2 years 3.60% less 20% tax = 2.9% (ECB MFI, Sep 2026)
fixed_income_return_high.note: High case: locking in 1-2 year deposits or Government savings notes after tax, allowing for some fall in rates.

life_claim_settlement_rate.note: The Bank of Lithuania (insurance supervisor) publishes market statistics but no industry-wide life claim settlement ratio could be found.

insurance_term_premium_table.note: Term life cover (rizikos gyvybės draudimas) is sold, but no regulator or other non-company published premium table per EUR 1,000 of cover was found.

health_hospitalisation_cost.note: Hospital care for people covered by compulsory health insurance (PSD) is paid by the National Health Insurance Fund; no official figure for the out-of-pocket cost of a major private hospital stay was found.

health_premium_table.note: Private health insurance is mostly employer-paid group cover; no published premium table per EUR 100,000 of cover was found.

goal_inflation_health.sourceName: Lithuania CPI, health: +5.7% year on year in September 2026 (Trading Economics, from State Data Agency); HICP health +3.8% in Dec 2025 (ECB)
goal_inflation_health.note: Health prices have been rising about as fast as or faster than headline prices, so 5% (two points above the 3% planning inflation) is used.

goal_inflation_education.sourceName: Lithuania CPI, education: +3.8% year on year in September 2026 (5.2% in August) (Trading Economics, from State Data Agency)
goal_inflation_education.note: Education costs are assumed to rise about 1.5 points above the 3% planning inflation, in line with recent education price growth.

life_expectancy.sourceName: Eurostat demo_mlexpec, life expectancy at birth, Lithuania
life_expectancy.note: 2024 figure (latest published; older than 2025): men 73.0, women 81.6. World Bank 2024 figure 77.2.

life_table_remaining.sourceName: Eurostat demo_mlexpec, life expectancy by age and sex, Lithuania
life_table_remaining.note: 2024 period life table (latest published; older than 2025).

support_ratio.sourceName: Eurostat EUROPOP2023 population projections, proj_23ndbi old-age dependency ratio (65+ to 15-64), baseline
support_ratio.note: 100 divided by the projected old-age dependency ratio: 33.4 in 2026, 46.3 in 2040, 67.8 in 2065. World Bank 2025 ratio 32.0 gives 3.1.

retirement_age_default.sourceName: TV3, pension guide (Sodra rules), updated 17 September 2026
retirement_age_default.note: Secondary source (Sodra pages could not be read): from 2026 men and women both reach old-age pension age at 65, the end of the phased rise; no further rise is legislated, so 65 applies to people born after 1975. A 15-year minimum record is needed and the full required record is 34.5 years in 2026 (35 from 2027).

retirement_age_government.note: Civil servants draw the general Sodra pension; the Civil Service Law sets an upper age limit for career civil servants (about 65), but the current consolidated text could not be read on e-seimas.lrs.lt.

retirement_return_low.sourceName: Household deposits up to 1 year 2.34% (ECB MFI, Sep 2026), assuming rates fall, less 20% tax
retirement_return_low.note: Low case: term deposit and savings-note rates drift lower.

retirement_return_base.sourceName: Household deposits up to 1 year 2.34% less 20% tax = 1.87% (ECB MFI, Sep 2026)
retirement_return_base.note: Base case capped at the after-tax 1-year term deposit rate.

retirement_return_high.sourceName: Household deposits over 1 and up to 2 years 3.60% less 20% tax = 2.9% (ECB MFI, Sep 2026)
retirement_return_high.note: High case: a ladder of 1-2 year deposits or Government savings notes after tax, allowing for some fall in rates.

retirement_accumulation_return_low.note: Low case for a balanced mix if shares lag.

retirement_accumulation_return_base.sourceName: After-tax safe rate about 2.1%; equity base 5.8%
retirement_accumulation_return_base.note: Base case: roughly half shares at 5.8% and half safe fixed income at about 2.1% after tax.

retirement_accumulation_return_high.note: High case for a growth-leaning balanced mix.

old_age_allowance_monthly.sourceName: TV3, pension guide: šalpos senatvės pensija (social assistance old-age pension) 2026
old_age_allowance_monthly.note: Secondary source (Sodra and ministry pages could not be read): EUR 261 a month in 2026, paid from the state budget to people of pension age who lack the 15-year minimum record and get no equal or larger social insurance pension.

old_age_allowance_eligibility.sourceName: TV3, pension guide (Sodra rules), updated 17 September 2026
old_age_allowance_eligibility.note: Paid from the old-age pension age (65 for men and women in 2026) to people without the minimum 15-year insurance record; it is not income-tested, but it is only paid when no equal or larger state social insurance pension is due (Law on Social Assistance Pensions, art. 7).

gratuity_rule.note: No per-year gratuity: under the Labour Code an employer pays severance of about two months' average wage on dismissal without the employee's fault (one year of service or more), with extra long-service benefits from the Long-term Employment Benefit Fund, which does not fit a days-per-year rule; the Labour Code text could not be read on e-seimas.lrs.lt.

public_pension_scheme.sourceName: TV3, pension guide (Sodra rules), updated 17 September 2026
public_pension_scheme.note: Sodra state social insurance old-age pension (general part plus individual part from points), payable from 65 with a 15-year minimum record; early pension up to 5 years sooner, cut 0.32% a month. Pensions are indexed each year in line with the growth of the wage bill rather than CPI. Tax treatment could not be confirmed from a readable official source.

dps.note: Monthly top-up savings deposits are offered by banks; no average rate is published.

sanchayapatra_5y.note: Sold to individuals in two-week issues with terms of up to 3 years (no 5-year term); the current rate could not be read from the Ministry of Finance site.

tbill_91d.note: No regular 3-month bill for retail investors was found.

tbond_5y.note: Domestic government bonds trade on the Vilnius exchange; no 5-year yield found.

equity_fund.note: Retail funds widely available; an investment account (investicinė sąskaita) defers tax on gains.

gold.note: No restriction on buying physical gold; investment gold is VAT-exempt under EU rules.

centralBank.name: Lietuvos bankas (Bank of Lithuania)
centralBank.note: Part of the Eurosystem; monetary policy set by the European Central Bank.

insuranceRegulator.name: Lietuvos bankas (Bank of Lithuania), financial market supervision

insuranceComplaints.name: Bank of Lithuania, disputes between consumers and financial market participants

pensionScheme.name: Sodra (State Social Insurance Fund Board), old-age pension

oldAgeAllowance.name: Šalpos senatvės pensija (social assistance old-age pension), paid through Sodra

publicHealthCover.name: Valstybinė ligonių kasa (National Health Insurance Fund), compulsory health insurance

depositInsurance.name: Indėlių ir investicijų draudimas (Deposit and Investment Insurance)
